provenance.sourceDataset: scripts/attention/candidates.json (sentences written for this toy, VIS-21)

parameters.contextPrefixNote: every sentence is preceded by GPT-2's <|endoftext|> token, as each document was in training and as the sampling data's prompts are. It is a real position, position 0, stored in each sentence's tokens, and the toy must show it: most heads put much of their attention on it.
parameters.weights: after the causal softmax. Stored as whole units of 1/10000 (0 to 10000), lower triangle only: for each sentence of t positions, 'weights' lists layer 0 head 0 row 0, then row 1 (2 entries), ..., row t-1 (t entries), then layer 0 head 1, and so on to layer 11 head 11. The entry for layer L, head H, row i, column j <= i is at (L * 12 + H) * t * (t + 1) / 2 + i * (i + 1) / 2 + j. Cells above the diagonal are not stored: GPT-2 cannot attend to a later position, so they are zero by construction, not measured.
parameters.rounding: each row is floored to units of 1/10000 and the units left over go to the largest remainders, so every row sums to exactly 10000 and every entry is within one unit of the float32 weight. Scores are computed from the float32 weights and rounded to 4 decimals; recomputed from the stored units, no head's above-or-below-threshold status changes (checked by extract.py and by data.test.ts).

measures.threshold: a head shows a behaviour on a sentence when its score is at least 0.5
measures.previousToken: mean of a[i][i-1] over positions i = 2 .. t-1 (position 1's previous token is position 0, which belongs to the sink)
measures.sink: mean of a[i][0] over positions i = 2 .. t-1, the same positions as previousToken; position 0 is <|endoftext|>
measures.induction: for each position q whose token appeared earlier, at p >= 1, with p + 1 < q - 1: the attention from q onto every such p + 1 (the token that followed the earlier copy), summed; averaged over those q
measures.duplicate: for each position q whose token appeared earlier, at p >= 1, with p < q - 1: the attention from q onto every such p (the earlier copy itself), summed; averaged over those q
measures.coreference: for each pronoun-antecedent pair written in candidates.json before the run: the attention from the pronoun onto all of the antecedent's tokens, summed; averaged over the pairs. Where a distractor (another noun the pronoun could have meant) is written, a head shows coreference only if it also gives the antecedent more than the distractor

parameters.selection: every candidate in scripts/attention/candidates.json that can be measured is shipped, whether or not GPT-2 shows the behaviour it targets; there is no selection by result. candidates.json beside this file lists them all.
parameters.predictionRule: a literature prediction 'holds' when the head shows the behaviour on at least half of the sentences that measure it, is 'partial' when it shows it on at least one, and is 'not seen' otherwise. A row whose 'tests' is 'not the claim' measures something its source did not say, so its result is 'not a test' whatever the counts. The result is this rule, not the source's: where a source ranks heads instead (wang2022's 'highest ... score' claims), the row's 'testsNote' says so and 'rankByMean' is the figure to set against that ranking. Every row carries its source's caveat ('where', from scripts/attention/predictions.json), and 'literatureCaveat' holds for all of them (VIS-56).
parameters.forwardPassCheck: scripts/attention/crosscheck.py against transformers 4.49.0 / torch 2.2.2 (GPT2Model, eager attention, output_attentions=True) on all 30 shipped sentences, 2026-10-05: same tokens, every one of the 144 heads' weights within 4.5e-6, about a tenth of the storage step
parameters.runningSentence: How many r's are in strawberry?

note: Every sentence run for the attention toy, with what it was written to show and what GPT-2's heads showed. Every one that could be measured is shipped in sentences.json; one whose target no head shows is kept, and listed here under targetsNotShown.

candidates.text: How many r's are in strawberry?
candidates.expect: The running sentence (doc-6). No token repeats, no pronoun: only previous-token and sink can be measured.

candidates.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
candidates.expect: 'The' and ' the' are different tokens, so no repeat.

candidates.text: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
candidates.expect: Plain fact.

candidates.text: Paris is the capital of France.
candidates.expect: Short plain fact.

candidates.text: Once upon a time, there lived a king.
candidates.expect: ' a' repeats, so induction and duplicate are measured too, from the second ' a'.

candidates.text: The cat sat on the mat.
candidates.expect: Short and common.

candidates.text: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday
candidates.expect: A list; ',' repeats, so induction is measured from each later comma onto the day after an earlier one.
Counting: each number is predictable from the one before.

candidates.text: She sells sea shells by the sea shore.
candidates.expect: The second ' sea' may look at ' shells', the token after the first ' sea' (induction), which here would predict the wrong word.

candidates.text: To be, or not to be, that is the question.
candidates.expect: ' be' and ',' repeat; 'To' and ' to' are different tokens.

candidates.text: for i in range(10): print(i)
candidates.expect: Code. '(' repeats; 'i' after '(' is a different token from ' i'.

candidates.text: green lamp seven river chair green lamp seven river chair
candidates.expect: A repeated list of unrelated words, the closest thing here to the random-token test in wang2022. The first 'green' has no space, so the repeat is matched from ' lamp' on.

candidates.text: apple, banana, cherry, apple, banana, cherry
candidates.expect: Repeated list; the first 'apple' has no space, so the repeat is matched from ',' and ' banana'.

candidates.text: Mr Dursley drove to work. Mr Dursley drove to work.
candidates.expect: A whole repeated sentence whose name splits into three tokens (' D', 'urs', 'ley').

candidates.text: When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to
candidates.expect: The indirect-object sentence of wang2022. The second ' John' is where their induction (5.5, 6.9) and duplicate (0.1, 3.0) heads act.

candidates.text: Anna met Ben at the station, and Anna
candidates.expect: One repeated name: induction from the second ' Anna' onto ' met'.
candidates.reason: cannot be measured: targets induction but no token repeats far enough back

candidates.text: Mary called John because she needed help.
candidates.expect: The pronoun's gender settles it.
candidates.reason: cannot be measured: ' Mary' occurs 0 times in 'Mary called John because she needed help.' as tokens [5335]

candidates.text: John called Mary because he needed help.
candidates.expect: The mirror of the one before.
candidates.reason: cannot be measured: ' John' occurs 0 times in 'John called Mary because he needed help.' as tokens [1757]

candidates.text: The king thanked the queen because he was grateful.
candidates.expect: Gender settles it, from nouns rather than names.

candidates.text: The queen thanked the king because she was grateful.
candidates.expect: The mirror of the one before.

candidates.text: Alice told Bob that she would arrive early.
candidates.expect: Gender settles it; the antecedent is the first word.
candidates.reason: cannot be measured: ' Alice' occurs 0 times in 'Alice told Bob that she would arrive early.' as tokens [14862]

candidates.text: Sarah lent her bike to Tom, and he rode it home.
candidates.expect: The antecedent is the nearer name. ' her' is not measured: there is no distractor before it, and a sentence's pairs either all have one or none do.
candidates.reason: cannot be measured: ' Sarah' occurs 0 times in 'Sarah lent her bike to Tom, and he rode it home.' as tokens [10490]

candidates.text: The dog chased the cat until it climbed a tree.
candidates.expect: No gender to go on: 'it' is the cat only from what dogs and cats do, and GPT-2 has read only 'until' when it reaches ' it'.

candidates.text: The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big.
candidates.expect: A Winograd schema. The word that decides it, ' big', comes after ' it', and GPT-2 cannot look ahead, so the attention from ' it' is the same as in the next sentence. One of the two must fail.

candidates.text: The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too small.
candidates.expect: The other half of the schema: same attention from ' it', opposite antecedent.

candidates.text: Emma bought a coat and she wore it.
candidates.expect: Two pronouns, two antecedents, no distractor for either.
candidates.reason: cannot be measured: ' Emma' occurs 0 times in 'Emma bought a coat and she wore it.' as tokens [18966]

candidates.text: My grandmother grows tomatoes in her small garden.
candidates.expect: No distractor: the only person before ' her'.

candidates.text: My sister lost her keys.
candidates.expect: Short; the antecedent is two tokens back.

candidates.text: The old man who lived next to the bakery said he was tired.
candidates.expect: The antecedent is eight tokens back, past a relative clause.

candidates.text: The boy gave his book to the girl.
candidates.expect: No distractor before ' his'; the girl comes after.

candidates.text: Mary called John because she needed help.
candidates.expect: Round 2: the round-1 candidate with the same text, its first word spelled without a leading space as GPT-2 tokenizes it. The pronoun's gender settles it.

candidates.text: John called Mary because he needed help.
candidates.expect: Round 2: the round-1 candidate with the same text, its first word spelled without a leading space as GPT-2 tokenizes it. The mirror of the one before.

candidates.text: Alice told Bob that she would arrive early.
candidates.expect: Round 2: the round-1 candidate with the same text, its first word spelled without a leading space as GPT-2 tokenizes it. Gender settles it; the antecedent is the first word.

candidates.text: Sarah lent her bike to Tom, and he rode it home.

candidates.text: Emma bought a coat and she wore it.
candidates.expect: Round 2: the round-1 candidate with the same text, its first word spelled without a leading space as GPT-2 tokenizes it. Two pronouns, two antecedents, no distractor for either.
